One of the tips I like to give newcomers to loading is, when using a standard three die rifle set, remove the decapping stem when full length sizing. This is especially true when dealing with range pickups, where you have no idea what the cases were fired in. Then, replace it and neck size on the compression stroke while also decapping.

Yes, this causes an extra step or two, but it does a couple of very important things for a newbie--it greatly reduces the chance for a stuck case, and it greatly facilitates the removal of a stuck case should it happen. It also helps build confidence in the lubing process.

A stuck case for a beginner is a discouraging event. They rarely ever have the proper tools to fix it, and wind up buggering up their dies.

I prefer an additional neck expanding/decapping die over having one die try to do three things (FL size, decap, neck expand). If it's military brass, I use a dedicated decapper as well as a dedicated neck expander.

Just my thoughts, would love to hear y'all's.
